facts.label: Loose dry sand: ultimate bearing capacity, 0.1 m^2 square foot at the surface
facts.display: ~37 kPa (range ~22-73 kPa) at first failure; rises as the foot sinks

sources.title: USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Bearing Capacity of Soils (1992), Tables 3-1, 4-1, 4-2, 4-4

facts.notes: My calculation, not a published value; both verifiers reproduced the arithmetic and table inputs. Terzaghi surface footing (Df=0), c'=0: q_ult = 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma*zeta_gamma, with B = sqrt(0.1 m^2) = 0.316 m and the square-footing factor zeta_gamma = 0.8 (EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-2). Inputs: gamma = 14-16 kN/m^3 and phi' = 28-34 deg, so Terzaghi N_gamma = 15.7-36.0 (Table 4-1). Central case phi' = 30 deg, gamma = 15 kN/m^3 (37.4 kPa). Low end: Vesic N_gamma = 16.72 at 28 deg with the 0.6 shape factor and gamma 14 (22.2 kPa). High end: 34 deg, gamma 16 (72.9 kPa). Editor caveat (from verifier): EM 1110-1-1905 states that local shear 'occurs in loose sands'; a textbook local-shear reduction (not in this EM, not verified here) could put first-failure capacity below the 22 kPa low end. For cohesionless soil q_ult grows roughly linearly with foot width B. Once the foot sinks, a surcharge term gamma*D*N_q is added: at 0.1 m embedment and 30 deg this is ~34 kPa with Terzaghi N_q = 22.46, ~43 kPa with Vesic N_q plus shape factor. A stomp sinks until capacity matches the load.

IBC/CBC Table 1806.2 Presumptive Load-Bearing Values (reproduction)

facts.notes: ALLOWABLE values, not ultimate: they include a safety factor and settlement limits and assume ordinary embedded footings. EM 1110-1-1905: 'For footings of width B < 3 ft ... the allowable bearing pressures is B times 1/3 of qna'. A 0.1 m^2 square foot is 1.037 ft wide, factor ~0.346, giving ~50 kPa for loose sand. The IBC table does not separate sand by density. Units: 1 ksf = 47,880 Pa; 1 psf = 47.88 Pa. Both verifiers confirmed.

facts.label: Loose sand: effective friction angle (shear strength tau = sigma' tan phi', c' = 0)

sources.title: USACE EM 1110-1-1905, Table 3-1b (Meyerhof 1974; Peck, Hanson & Thornburn 1974)

facts.notes: Table 3-1b gives loose sand (Dr 20-40%, N60 4-10) as 29-30 deg (Peck, Hanson & Thornburn) or 30-35 deg (Meyerhof). Very loose is below 29-30 deg. Dry sand has no cohesion, so its shear strength depends on stress: tau = sigma' * tan(phi'); it cannot be given as a single Pa value. The 28 deg low bound is slightly below the tabulated loose band, covering very loose sand.

facts.label: Loose dry sand: effective traction coefficient for a clawed, scaly foot

sources.title: Basis: friction angle from USACE EM 1110-1-1905 Table 3-1b
Concept only: Dai, Gorb & Schwarz (2002) Roughness-dependent friction force of the tarsal claw system in the beetle Pachnoda marginata, J Exp Biol 205:2479-2488

facts.notes: Estimate; no measured keratin-claw-on-sand data found. Reasoning: claws penetrate and interlock with the sand, so slip happens by shearing the sand under the foot rather than by keratin sliding on grains; the limit is then about mu_eff ~ tan(phi') = 0.53-0.62 for phi' = 28-32 deg. Dai et al. (2002, beetle claws) report that when surface roughness/particle size is much larger than the claw tip the claw interlocks mechanically, and when it is comparable or smaller, contact friction governs; this supports the concept only, not the number. Passive resistance in front of buried toes and claws can add somewhat. A very hard push excavates the sand instead of moving the dinosaur.

facts.label: Dense sand / gravel: ultimate bearing capacity, 0.1 m^2 square foot at the surface
facts.notes: My calculation; both verifiers reproduced it. Terzaghi surface square footing: q_ult = 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma*0.8 with B = 0.316 m. Low: phi' = 36 deg, gamma = 18 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 52.0) -> 118 kPa. Central: phi' = 40 deg, gamma = 19 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 100.4) -> 241 kPa. High: very dense gravel, phi' = 44 deg, gamma = 20 kN/m^3 (N_gamma = 257) -> 650 kPa. Editor caveat (from verifier): high-phi N_gamma values are known to overestimate capacity for small footings (scale effect), so the high end is optimistic. The result is very sensitive to phi' and grows linearly with foot width. Any embedment adds the gamma*D*N_q term, which is large (N_q = 81.27 at 40 deg).

facts.label: Asphalt pavement on compacted base: ultimate bearing under a 0.1 m^2 foot

sources.title: Context only: tyre-pressure categories (Fiji CAA AIC 04/25)

facts.notes: Order-of-magnitude estimate only; no published ultimate static punch capacity found. Reasoning: high-category airfield pavements carry tyre pressures up to 1.75 MPa in repeated service, so the single-load ultimate is plausibly higher. The asphalt and base spread the load onto the subgrade, which ultimately governs. Asphalt is viscoelastic: much weaker when hot and under sustained load (rutting) than when cold and under rapid load. facts.label: Asphalt: friction coefficient, keratin scales/claws

sources.title: Concept only: Dai, Gorb & Schwarz (2002) Roughness-dependent friction force of the tarsal claw system, J Exp Biol 205:2479-2488 (no keratin-on-asphalt numbers)

facts.notes: Estimate; no measured data. Dai et al. report claws interlock mechanically when surface roughness is much larger than the claw tip diameter, and contact friction governs when roughness is comparable or smaller. Reasoning: dry asphalt's coarse macrotexture lets claw tips catch on aggregate, giving roughly rubber-like grip. Wet surfaces lower. facts.label: Concrete local bearing (crushing) strength per ACI 318 (nominal)
facts.display: B_n = 0.85 f'c A1 sqrt(A2/A1), sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2 (max 1.7 f'c); design phi = 0.65

sources.title: University lecture on footing design citing ACI 318 (former section 10.14) bearing check, with worked example

facts.notes: Verifiers disagreed on the cap. Editor settled it by extracting the lecture text: its general paragraph says 'The ratio A2/A1 < 2', but its worked example states 'ACI Code Section 10.14 indicates that the bearing strength should be at least 0.85 phi f'c A1 sqrt(A2/A1) with a limit of sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2', computes sqrt(A2/A1) = 6.28 > 2, 'Take sqrt(A2/A1) = 2', and uses the factor 2. So the earlier sentence is a slip and the cap is sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2 (max 1.7 f'c). Caveat: this is a secondary source and the ACI code text itself was not opened. A1 is the loaded area and A2 the geometrically similar supporting area; a foot on a large slab gets the full factor 2. Value: 1.7 x 24.13 MPa = 41.0 MPa (nominal, before phi). Low: 0.85 x 17.24 MPa (no confinement benefit). High: 1.7 x 27.58 MPa. Real crushing under a confined punch can be higher. In practice a slab-on-grade punches through or cracks in flexure long before the surface crushes (see next entries).

facts.label: Concrete two-way (punching) shear stress capacity, ACI 318 (reinforced slabs)
facts.display: v_c = 4 lambda sqrt(f'c) psi = 0.33 lambda sqrt(f'c) MPa (smallest of three ACI expressions); critical perimeter b0 at d/2 from the loaded area

sources.title: StructurePoint: GammaF in two-way slab punching shear (ACI 318-14, 22.6.4.1)
University lecture (SI form Vc = 0.33 sqrt(f'c) b0 d for punching)

facts.notes: v_c = min(4, 2 + 4/beta, alpha_s*d/b0 + 2) x lambda*sqrt(f'c) psi (ACI 318-14). Values for f'c = 17.24-27.58 MPa (central 24.13 MPa). Currency: ACI 318-19 adds a size-effect factor lambda_s to two-way shear; both verifiers recall it equals 1 for d up to about 10 in (250 mm), which would leave slab-scale values unchanged, but this was NOT verified. This is for structural two-way slabs; plain slabs-on-ground are designed differently (see next entry).

facts.label: Slab-on-grade: average foot pressure to punch through (0.1 m^2 foot)
facts.display: ~2.5 MPa for a 100 mm residential slab (~1.5 MPa if plain-concrete shear limits apply) up to ~7.2 MPa for a 200 mm, 27.6 MPa slab

sources.title: Formula basis: ACI 318 two-way shear (StructurePoint)
f'c range: Minnesota Rules 1309.0402 (IRC R402.2)

facts.notes: Calculation, not a published value: V = k*sqrt(f'c)*b0*h, b0 = 4(B + h), B = 0.316 m, pressure = V/0.1 m^2. Verifiers split (arithmetic confirmed vs. method questioned); editor revised the range rather than the method. Central: 100 mm slab, f'c 20.68 MPa, k = 4 sqrt(psi) (0.33 sqrt(MPa)) -> V ~ 251 kN, 2.5 MPa (17.24 MPa gives 230 kN, 2.3 MPa). Low (new): the same 100 mm slab at 17.24 MPa with k = 2.66 sqrt(psi), the ACI plain-concrete two-way limit as both verifiers recall it (NOT verified) -> 153 kN, 1.5 MPa; this also roughly covers the overstatement from using full thickness h as effective depth d. High (revised): the researcher's 8 MPa used f'c = 34.5 MPa, above the verified f'c range, so it is recomputed at 27.58 MPa: 200 mm slab -> 720 kN, 7.2 MPa (150 mm -> 488 kN, 4.9 MPa). Caveats: ACI 318 is a structural-slab code and slabs-on-ground are normally designed to other guidance (ACI 360, not checked); subgrade reaction inside the perimeter raises capacity; flexural cracking may come first; after cracking the slab acts as broken plates on the subgrade.

facts.label: Rock under a small punch: ultimate bearing / UCS (confinement factor)
facts.display: q_ult ~ (N_phi + 1) x UCS (strip) x 1.25 (square); N_phi = tan^2(45 + phi/2) -> ~8.5-14 for intact rock; lower bound ~1 x UCS

sources.title: USACE EM 1110-1-2908 Rock Foundations (1994), Eqs 6-2, 6-4, 6-5, 6-7 and Table 6-1

facts.notes: Derived from EM 1110-1-2908 equations (both verifiers confirmed the equations and algebra): local-shear q_ult = c*N_c (+ 0.5*gamma*B*N_gamma), N_c = 2*N_phi^0.5*(N_phi + 1). Intact-rock lower-bound cohesion c = q_u/(2*tan(45 + phi/2)) (Eq 6-7a, s = 1). Together: q_ult ~ q_u*(N_phi + 1) for a strip, x1.25 for a square (Sowers). For an ASSUMED intact friction angle phi = 45-55 deg (unsourced), N_phi = 5.83-10.06, factor 6.8-11.1 (strip) or 8.5-13.8 (square). Poorly confined, jointed rock columns fail near unconfined strength (Eq 6-5: 2c*tan(45 + phi/2) = q_u), so the factor drops toward 1. The q_ult = q_u(N_phi + 1) attribution to Goodman (1989) was not checked.
facts.who_when: Estimate built on USACE EM 1110-1-2908 (30 Nov 1994)

Krakatoa 1883: no sourced energy RANGE; only the single ~200 Mt figure via Wikipedia (citing a removed BoM page and a 2007 popular book).

Keratin claw/scale friction on every surface: no measured data; all traction coefficients are reasoned estimates. Dai, Gorb & Schwarz (2002, beetle claws) is cited for the interlocking-vs-roughness mechanism only.

ACI 318 primary code text not opened: the bearing cap sqrt(A2/A1) <= 2 is confirmed only by a university lecture's worked example; the ACI 318-19 two-way shear size-effect factor lambda_s, the plain-concrete two-way shear limit (~2.66 sqrt(f'c) psi, used for the slab punch-through low bound), and ACI 360 slab-on-ground methods were not verified.
Composition B TNT equivalence: only Wikipedia's RE factor table (1.33, tagged 'citation needed'); the M67 TNT-equivalent energy (~1.0 MJ) is therefore an estimate.
Dissociation onset temperatures for O2 and N2 (commonly quoted ~2,000-2,500 K and ~4,000 K at 1 atm) not verified; Wikipedia's ~2000 K for nitrogen is citation-needed and was not used.

Earth gravitational binding energy: PREM-based 2.49e32 J not reproduced (Wikipedia only).
Collins et al. (2017) revised airblast model not checked; the 2005 fits are used.
